title: Embayu: roomy three-bedroom units beside HELP University.
excerpt: A completed three-block project near HELP University and the DASH highway, with a garden entrance and generous common areas, but deep, dark 1,000 sq ft units and new supply all around.
takeaways: Three-bedroom, 1,000 sq ft units at about RM480,000 to RM500,000 in subsale.
A landscaped arrival, wide corridors and a big facility deck on top of the car park.
Deep units that rely on artificial light, an exposed walk to facilities and lots of new supply nearby.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Embayu has three low blocks, kept short by the nearby airport, set around a shared car park whose roof is the facility deck, with a lap pool, kids' pool, playground, hall and a gym facing the pool. Launched when land was cheaper, it has car parks on the ground and generous common areas: a 3.3 m-wide lift lobby and 1.75 m corridors lit through a large void.
The 1,000 sq ft, three-bedroom Type A is long and narrow, with only the master bedroom on the facade, a 2.9 m ceiling and a yard. Some units have balconies and some don't.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It sits on a stretch of shop offices leading to HELP University, now joined by an international school, with shops, clinics and tuition centres a short walk away. The DASH highway reaches Kota Damansara in about ten minutes, and the Subang airport is close, but peak traffic towards Ara Damansara and PJ is heavy.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Subsale prices are about RM480,000 to RM500,000 for the 1,000 sq ft unit, which was being offered for rent at about RM2,900 a month. Sean, who attended the launch, says early buyers have done well as the area matured around HELP and the DASH highway.

standout.title: A garden where the car park would be
standout.body: Instead of driving straight into a car park podium, residents arrive at a landscaped garden with a koi pond between the entrance and the car park, linked to the facility deck by a see-through steel staircase. Sean finds it very refreshing, a little escape before you reach your unit.

pros: The unusual car park and common areas: ground-floor parking and a shared elevated car park linked to each block at an angle, with a green space by the drop-off rising by steel stairs to the deck, unlike the usual podium under a tower.
A big sense of space: wide corridors and lift lobbies, a grand drop-off and a large, simple facility deck on the car park roof without a long list of facilities.
Value for early buyers: Sean was at the launch, before the DASH highway opened, and the area has since matured around HELP University, making rents of RM2,900 to RM3,000 a good return.
cons: Competition: since the DASH highway opened, new projects at similar prices, one under construction opposite and one nearly complete, target the same students and workers, with more empty land to fill.
The unit layout: deep, narrow units with dark inner spaces, wasted corridor space, a large column in the kitchen, a mix of balcony and no-balcony units, and facing units in the L-shaped blocks.

The massing: a small pool, an exposed walk to facilities and car parks in the rain or sun, low units facing the car park walls, and, with the height limit, future neighbouring slabs could block views.

closing: Sean calls it beyond expectation and superb value, as long as the address makes sense for your daily life.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this June 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. Sean viewed an owner's completed unit, whose kitchen was fitted by The Makeover Guys, a furnishing company Sean works with.
